source.timeline: PR #17751 introduced the asynchronous KV-transfer lifecycle. During review of HMA/NIXL work in PR #32204, maintainers identified that reconstructing an exact external hit count from allocated blocks assumes block alignment. PR #34616 isolated and fixed that accounting problem and superseded the narrower full-block proposal in PR #32168. No public issue is linked.

cutoff_policy.scope: The cutoff applies to the repository Base, repository dependencies, and task-specific tools or runtime assets. General build and runtime tools such as Python, uv, Rust, cargo, cargo-nextest, and system build packages are exempt.

instruction_reproduction.entrypoint: production Scheduler with a verifier-owned KVConnectorBase_V1 implementation
instruction_reproduction.trace_note: These values were read from the real Scheduler and SchedulerOutput in the pinned image. They are a curator-recorded state trace, not text emitted by vLLM's built-in logger.

verifier_contract.scope: Device-independent exact computed-token accounting across a single-group asynchronous external KV load, with adjacent zero-hit, synchronous, aligned, full-prompt, failure, prefix-cache, cancellation, local-plus-external, and concurrent behavior preserved.
verifier_contract.collection_integrity: Exactly 24 unique behavior cases with zero failures, errors, or skips are required, followed by a separate reduced cross-process lifecycle program.

real_stages: connector metadata creation and cross-process serialization
worker-side connector creation and asynchronous completion
scheduler completion handling and SchedulerOutput generation
substituted_stages: a verifier-owned AsyncMemoryConnector replaces a production external KV backend
a multiprocessing Queue replaces the engine/executor result channel
an empty ModelRunnerOutput replaces model execution
reduced_end_to_end.why_semantics_are_preserved: The defect is the scheduler's conversion of an exact connector-reported token count into runner accounting after async completion. It does not depend on tensor contents, a model forward pass, GPU execution, or backend transport semantics.
reduced_end_to_end.hidden_variations: Three requests with prompt lengths 58, 81, and 113, match counts 7, 34, and 65, and staggered completion delays are absent from the instruction.
reduced_end_to_end.limitation: This validates the scheduler/connector contract and process boundary, not a production connector, real KV data movement, EngineCore transport, or model inference.

adversarial_runs.planned_defect: Drops the local prefix when deriving the final count.
Fails to schedule one token after a full prompt hit.
Changes only the reported runner field while leaving scheduler state wrong.
Attempts to skip verifier cases through a repository conftest.
Stores the exact count while waiting but overwrites it from allocated blocks on completion.

alternative_implementation_runs.change: Keeps exact async counts in a scheduler-owned per-request ledger and cleans the ledger on success, failure, and cancellation instead of storing the pending count on Request as Oracle does.

critical_review_rounds: direct source PR, discovery PR, superseded proposal, comments, inline review, and squash-parent relationship checked
instruction trace reproduced on Base and Oracle through the same scheduler/connector boundary
Oracle narrowed to exact token accounting and a scheduler-ledger alternative added
24 behavior cases, reduced cross-process lifecycle, six adversarial controls, and five-round Base/Oracle stability checked
Git, dependency, network, final-filesystem, and all-layer isolation checked
